messages:
Lina: deploy-bot just flagged canary p95 +300ms vs baseline, recommends fallback. canary slice = eu-west1; rolling 20% -> 100% yesterday.

deploy-bot: ALERT: Canary latency regression detected (p95 +312ms). Suggested action: hold rollout and consider manual revert. See /deploy/7664 for details. :warning:

Mike: copy. is this across all models or one variant?

Sasha: looks like it’s the new kv-cache kernel on v3.2.1-alpha. only affects requests with >512 tokens. I pushed a quick perf diff earlier.

Jamal: can we pin traffic back to 3.1.8 without customer-visible churn? what’s the rollback blast radius?

Eva: pinning is safe — no schema/db bump in this release. customers on dedicated pools unaffected. hosted clients will see slightly lower throughput during traffic shift (~2m).

Lina: ops-oncall can you start the manual-cutover checklist if we decide to revert? we should also draft a short release-note update and customer note.

ops-oncall: starting checklist. tagging runbook and preparing play: 
```
# Manual rollback steps (short)
1) Set release pin for hosted -> model: v3.1.8
2) Update traffic-slice: canary->0, default->v3.1.8
3) Watch ingest queues and p95 for 15m
4) Notify customers + CS
5) Unpin when stable
```

Mike: for the pin command: `rbctl pin model inference:v3.1.8 --scope=hosted --reason="canary latency regression"`

Sasha: confirm that v3.1.8 uses legacy kv-cache path (yes). also we should disable the new kernel flag on dev and run a regression test before re-promoting.

Lina: decision: we do a manual rollback now. Jamal, want to take lead on executing step 1-2? I’ll handle comms and release-note snippet.

Jamal: taking it. executing pin now.

deploy-bot: ACTION: Pin command received by rbctl user=jamal at 2026-03-21T14:07:30Z. Applying pin to hosted.

Jamal: ran: `rbctl pin model inference:v3.1.8 --scope=hosted --reason="canary p95 regression"` -> exit 0. starting traffic switch to v3.1.8, will route 100% within 90s.

Sasha: good. I’ll roll back the kernel flag in staging and run the targeted perf job in parallel.

Eva: drafting customer note: "We detected a latency regression in a canary deployment and have safely rolled back to the previous model. No action required from customers; we're monitoring."
Short CS blurb ready to paste.

Lina: release-note patch: add line under Changes: "Rolled back kv-cache kernel change due to p95 regressions in canary; will reintroduce after further validation."

ops-oncall: traffic at 100% v3.1.8. p95 back to baseline (+8ms). queues normal. monitoring for 30m.

Mike: nice. post-mortem owners? Sasha for kernel work, Jamal for deploy runbook tweaks, Lina for comms + release notes.

Sasha: noted. I'll open an eval ticket with regression test cases and a binary diff. link coming.

Jamal: filed TKT-5112: rollback-exec + deploy hint improvements. includes improved `rbctl` dry-run output.

Lina: thanks everyone. CS notified, release note updated, ops will keep an eye. After 60m we can close this thread. :thumbsup:

ops-oncall: monitoring 60m window. if anything regresses we'll reopen and escalate.
